findings.fix: Make step 1 one procedure: name the question, pick the row in authoring-rules.md section 1, and ask only when the named type cannot represent the facts (the rule already in section 1). Drop the 'equally plausible' ask so the agent does not stop on a type the table already decides.

findings.evidence: NEVER leave out or mark optional the reply... then 'A high-level overview may omit replies on purpose; say so. A syntax-only repair never adds reply edges.'
findings.fix: Split the reply rule into the failure and the exception: NEVER omit a reply on a call-by-call sequence when the facts show one; the high-level overview and the syntax-only repair are the only exceptions, and both must be named in the reply. Keep the fact that an unbalanced activation and a label-as-id fail silently.

findings.evidence: Step 5: '`--` identifying when that FK is part of the child's PK ... `..` non-identifying otherwise' while the Mermaid docs define `..` as non-identifying and `--` as identifying, so a model that follows the vendor page draws the opposite line
findings.fix: Put the vendor conflict in the step: Mermaid's own ER page (https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/entityRelationshipDiagram.html) calls `..` non-identifying and `--` identifying. This skill's rule is the inverse and is intentional; say so in the reply when the diagram is for a reader who knows the Mermaid docs, and keep the parent-to-child glyph table.
